chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Muhammad ibn Hanan al-Jallab from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who buys one hundred sheep on the condition that he exchanges them for such and such. He said, 'It is not permissible.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying sheep with a condition to exchange them for other specific sheep?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of conditional livestock exchange (mubadala), ruling it invalid likely due to the uncertainty (gharar) inherent in swapping unspecified future goods for a specific purchase. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity in commodity transactions to avoid disputes over quality and quantity, a key principle in the chapter of buying animals.
